free_text_notes.physician_note: 81-year-old woman with prior TIA, hypertension, admitted 4/8 with left MCA ischemic stroke with mild right hemiparesis. MRI confirmed small infarct; no hemorrhagic conversion.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Slept well overnight. Voiding without difficulty. Therapy referral still needs to be sent. Mild anaemia was found on admission blood work. It has been stable throughout the stay and does not affect discharge readiness. A skin integrity check was performed on admission as per standard protocol. No pressure sores or skin concerns were identified during the stay.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: Plan is discharge home with daughter. 4/12 17:00: Team decision tonight: atorvastatin changed from 20 mg daily to 80 mg daily. Daughter called asking about the plan and does not know about the change; has not been able to reach the physician. Patient worried about the cost of the new medication. Original evening van slot cancelled; family will drive at the planned discharge time instead. Physician is swamped. Can the system just message the patient and daughter about the atorvastatin change directly?
